production_reaction: Co-59(n,γ)Co-60; threshold for fast neutron reaction Co-59(n,p)Fe-59
source_material_in_reactor: Structural steel containing 0.01-0.05% cobalt; reactor vessel steel; piping; RBMK steel pressure tubes (~7800 tonnes steel in reactor building)
status_2026: ~99.4% decayed; negligible by 2026 (~7.6 half-lives = factor 195 reduction); dominated dose rate in sarcophagus 1986-2010
dose_significance: Primary structural activation dose contributor 1986-2010; 1173+1332 keV gammas used for Co-60 monitoring in shelter workers; now essentially gone; Ni-63 dominates current structural activation inventory
source: NUREG/CR-3474 OSTI; Kleszcz Mietelski 2010 Radiochimica Acta doi:10.1524/ract.2010.1727

source_material_in_reactor: Nickel-containing steel alloys in reactor; Ni-58 is most abundant Ni isotope (68%)
status_2026: Fully decayed by ~1990 (~10+ half-lives from 70 days = decayed within 2 years); contributed to early high dose rates in cooling circuits
dose_significance: Short-lived structural activation; important 1986-1988 for worker dose in cooling circuit maintenance; irrelevant now

production_reaction: Fe-54(n,p)Mn-54; fast neutron reaction on iron
source_material_in_reactor: Structural steel (iron main component); 5.8% natural Fe-54 abundance
status_2026: Fully decayed by ~1990-1991 (~5 years = ~6 half-lives); contributed significantly to 1986-1988 dose in reactor building and cooling circuit workers
dose_significance: High initial activity; 835 keV gamma penetrating; important 1986-1990; now gone

source_material_in_reactor: Structural steel (98% iron); very high reaction rate due to abundant Fe-54
status_2026: Fully decayed by ~1992-1993 (~11 half-lives elapsed by 2026); pure EC decay with X-rays only; soft X-ray not penetrating; primarily an ingestion/inhalation dose concern 1986-1992; difficult to measure
dose_significance: Soft tissue dose from ingested iron-55; relevant for reactor workers who ingested contaminated water/food 1986-1990; non-penetrating so not a direct external hazard

source_material_in_reactor: Nickel in steel alloys; stainless steel may contain 8-12% Ni; reactor steam pipes pressure vessels
status_2026: ~36% of original 1986 activity remains; still present in structural materials of shelter; co-produced with Co-60 confirmed in Chernobyl hot particles; pure beta emitter (no gamma)
dose_significance: Long-term structural contamination concern; pure beta (low energy 0.065 MeV max) so not external hazard; leaching into groundwater possible; relevant for long-term waste management of shelter structural steel
source: Kleszcz Mietelski 2010 Radiochimica Acta; NUREG/CR-3474; NNDC

status_2026: Essentially no decay by 2026 (<0.001% decay in 40 years); extremely long-lived; contributes to very long-term contamination of structural steel
dose_significance: Essentially permanent activation product in reactor structures; relevant for decommissioning and long-term waste classification; EC to stable Co-59 with Auger electrons only

production_reaction: Nb-93(n,γ)Nb-94; Nb-93 may first become Nb-93m which has t1/2=16yr before activating
source_material_in_reactor: Niobium in zircaloy RBMK fuel rod cladding (1% Nb stabilizer in Zr-Nb alloy); ~1660 fuel channels × 18m length each = significant Zr mass
status_2026: No detectable decay by 2026 (t1/2=20300yr; only 40yr elapsed = 0.0002% decay); effectively permanent; gamma emitter; becomes increasingly important relative to shorter-lived isotopes after Co-60 decays away
dose_significance: Low activity but very long-lived; after Co-60 decays (~80yr) Nb-94 will be significant structural activation dose contributor; key isotope for 100-year and 1000-year waste management planning for shelter and decommissioning
source: NUREG/CR-3474 OSTI:6776358; NNDC; Kashparov 2020; reactor structure activation

production_reaction: Zn-64(n,γ)Zn-65; natural Zn in brass fittings and galvanized components
source_material_in_reactor: Zinc in reactor cooling circuit components; brass valve fittings; galvanized pipes
status_2026: Fully decayed by ~1990-1991; 60th half-life by 2026; contributed to dose in cooling circuit workers 1986-1988; 1115 keV penetrating gamma
dose_significance: Important in cooling circuit water chemistry 1986-1988; 1115 keV gamma easily detected; activated zinc in cooling water carried dose out of reactor; decayed fully by 1990

production_reaction: N-14(n,p)C-14 from nitrogen dissolved in coolant water; O-17(n,α)C-14 from oxygen in UO2
source_material_in_reactor: Nitrogen impurities in cooling water; oxygen in UO2 fuel matrix
status_2026: Essentially no decay (< 0.5% in 40yr); very long-lived; dispersed globally as CO2 through reactor operation AND explosion release; global atmospheric C-14 inventory
dose_significance: Pure beta emitter (0.156 MeV max); dispersed as CO2; global dilution means negligible dose individually; relevant for atmospheric carbon budget; nuclear testing released far more C-14 than Chernobyl (213000 PBq from testing vs small release from accident)

production_reaction: Li-6(n,α)H-3; also D-2(n,γ)H-3 in heavy water impurities; fast neutron on O-16
source_material_in_reactor: Trace lithium in steel; deuterium in water; Li-6 enriched absorbers
status_2026: ~99.7% decayed by 2026; soft beta emitter (0.019 MeV max); was relevant in cooling water 1986-1998; tritiated water released in groundwater; currently negligible in CEZ
dose_significance: Soft beta no gamma; tritiated water is main pathway; biological half-life 12 days (as HTO); relevant in 1986-1998 for reactor workers handling cooling water; effectively gone from shelter now

production_reaction: Am-243(n,γ)Cm-244; and Pu-243(β-)Am-243(n,γ)Cm-244; in-core transmutation chain
source_material_in_reactor: Formed by successive neutron captures in uranium fuel during 3-year fuel irradiation period
status_2026: ~89% decayed; ~11% remains; alpha emitter; contributes to alpha contamination in corium; ingrowth to Pu-240 and Pu-236 daughters
dose_significance: Alpha emitter in corium; not significant outside corium mass; relevant for workers handling corium directly; Cm-244 is the main curium isotope from nuclear fuel
source: NNDC; corium composition estimates from nuclear fuel burnup codes

production_reaction: Eu-153(n,γ)Eu-154; europium is trace rare earth impurity in fuel or activation of structural materials
source_material_in_reactor: Trace europium in fuel matrix; rare earth impurities; sometimes used as burnable poison
status_2026: ~98% decayed; some remains; 1274 keV gamma; activated by thermal neutrons in REE impurities; detected in soil surveys as proxy for fuel particle presence (REE do not volatilize)
dose_significance: Used as tracer for fuel particle location in environmental surveys; 1274 keV gamma penetrating and easily identified in Ge spectra; detected in Chernobyl zone soil samples 1986-2005

source_material_in_reactor: Corium (FCM) contains fission product and actinide inventory overwhelmingly dominates over structural activation products
estimated_initial_activity_1986_Bq: Total shelter radioactive inventory is >>99% from fuel/fission products and actinides; structural activation products (Co-60 Ni-63 Nb-94 etc.) contribute <1% of total disintegrations; but activation products in structural steel outside corium zones are relevant for decommissioning waste classification
estimated_activity_2026_Bq: By 2026: corium Cs-137=~remaining fraction of 85 PBq × 0.4 (decay); Sr-90=~10 PBq × 0.38; Am-241 growing from Pu-241; activation products (Ni-63 Ni-59 Nb-94 C-14) all low activity but relevant for 100-10000yr waste planning
